author: barnabemonnot
content:
<@931591385545584640> several points in there. PQ will not really land with decoupled consensus if that went in I-star, even as it is being prepared actively in parallel for landing on the available chain for J-star (https://ethresear.ch/t/why-ethereum-needs-a-dynamically-available-protocol/24418#p-59055-a-near-term-benefit-post-quantum-readiness-and-post-quantum-heartbeat-6) So in my view, landing faster slots in Hegotá doesn't actively keep dev cycles away from PQ.

Second, the way we'd like to move forward with faster slots requires one upfront cost of making the slot time more of a parameter in specs and client code. It is very likely that doing this in I-star, along with decoupled consensus, is unreasonable, given the size of decoupled consensus. Meaning the earliest we could get the machinery in place to shorten slots would be Hegotá, with J-star as the next opportunity. Then "There will be space in the roadmap over the coming forks to look at shorting slots" is in my view too optimistic.

Third, it is my impression that the PQ crowd at EF generally supports a moderate slot time decrease for Hegotá (eg, 10 seconds), including the upfront work of laying out the machinery for changing the slot time in the first place.
